items.content_html:
Summary

  • Restructure the X-Content-Type-Options page to explain both behaviors of nosniff:
    • Request blocking for script/style destinations (Fetch spec)
    • MIME type sniffing disabled for other response types including HTML documents (MIME Sniffing spec)
  • Fix the misleading NOTE that implied nosniff only applies to script/style request blocking
  • Update the nosniff directive description to cover both behaviors
  • Add guidance that servers should always send an accurate Content-Type

Fixes #41745
Continues the work from #41776.

Test plan

  • Spec links to Fetch and MIME Sniffing specifications resolve correctly
  • Description accurately reflects both spec behaviors
  • No grammar issues (fixes "only apply" → restructured)

🤖 Generated with Claude Code

Summary

  • Add a "Client-side considerations" section to the CORS errors landing page covering three strategies: avoiding preflight via simple requests, using no-cors mode for opaque responses, and proxy servers
  • Add a "If you don't control the server" section to the CORSMissingAllowOrigin error page pointing to these client-side alternatives

The CORS error documentation focuses entirely on server-side fixes. Developers who don't control the server have no guidance. A maintainer commented "Please feel free to change this doc in whatever way you feel appropriate."

Fixes #39378.

  • CORSMissingAllowOrigin page renders with new section

items.content_html:
Summary

  • Add documentation pages for type() instance method on WebAssembly.Memory, WebAssembly.Table, and WebAssembly.Global
  • These methods are part of the WebAssembly js-types proposal and return objects describing the type of each construct
  • List type() in each object's instance methods section on their parent pages
  • Follows the existing format established by WebAssembly.Tag.prototype.type()

Motivation

The js-types proposal adds type() methods to Memory, Table, and Global, but only Tag.type() is currently documented on MDN. The issue notes these methods are implemented in Safari and meet MDN's documentation criteria.

Fixes #41157.

Test plan

  • New pages render correctly
  • Browser compatibility tables load (via browser-compat keys)
  • Parent page instance method lists link correctly
items.title: Document type() method for Memory, Table, and Global

items.content_html:
Summary

  • Add a Description section to the backdrop-filter CSS property page explaining that effects are bounded by the nearest ancestor backdrop root
  • List the properties that create a backdrop root: filter, opacity, mask, mask-image, mask-border, clip-path, backdrop-filter, mix-blend-mode, and will-change
  • Explain the common confusion when backdrop-filter appears to have no effect due to an ancestor backdrop root

Motivation

Developers are frequently confused when backdrop-filter doesn't affect all pixels behind an element. The concept of a "backdrop root" (from Filter Effects Level 2) is not documented on MDN. A previous PR (#40627) attempted this but was closed due to merge conflicts; this is a fresh implementation incorporating reviewer feedback (using a dedicated Description section instead of a note).

Fixes #40602.

Test plan

  • Page renders correctly with new Description section
  • All CSS property links resolve
items.title: Document backdrop root concept on backdrop-filter page

Summary

  • Add a new guide page (Web/Performance/Guides/bfcache) explaining the back/forward cache
  • Covers: how bfcache works, bfcache vs HTTP caching (RFC 9111 Section 6), stale content handling via pageshow, what blocks bfcache (unload, no-store, open connections), monitoring with notRestoredReasons, and best practices
  • Links the guide from the Performance landing page and the bfcache glossary entry

Motivation

The bfcache glossary entry is brief and doesn't cover how bfcache interacts with HTTP caching, what blocks it, or how to handle stale content. A maintainer requested a full guide page under Web/Performance.

As requested in #41211.

Test plan

  • New page renders correctly
  • All internal links resolve
  • Performance landing page link works
  • Glossary entry links work

items.content_html:
Summary

  • Add a new guide page (Web/API/Push_API/Web_Push_Architecture) explaining how the Web Push infrastructure works end-to-end
  • Covers: subscription flow, push services (Mozilla Autopush, FCM, Apple), message encryption (RFC 8291), VAPID authentication (RFC 8292), delivery headers (TTL, Urgency, Topic), response codes, and subscription lifecycle
  • Links the new guide from the Push API landing page's See Also section

Motivation

The existing Push API docs explain the JavaScript interfaces but not the underlying architecture. Developers need to understand VAPID, encryption, and the delivery protocol to build a working implementation.

As requested in #39747.

Test plan

  • New page renders correctly
  • All internal links resolve
  • See Also link from Push API landing page works

Description

The MDN page for Event.isTrusted property suggests that the click event should always have the property set to false. This seems incorrect.

Motivation

All of Blink, Gecko and WebKit fire clicks with regular .isTrusted values (trusted if and only if the event came from UA).

Additional details

Related issues and pull requests

See w3c/pointerevents#642.

items.content_html:
Make HTTP/1.0 examples conform to the spec.

https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc1945#section-4.1

Full-Request and Full-Response use the generic message format of RFC 822 for transferring entities. Both messages may include optional header fields (also known as "headers") and an entity body. The entity body is separated from the headers by a null line (i.e., a line with nothing preceding the CRLF).
items.title: Add blank line between headers and body in HTTP/1.0 examples
